Acknowledgement of Country

The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority proudly acknowledges and pays respect to Victoria’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and their rich and enduring cultures.

We acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as Australia’s first peoples and as the Traditional Owners and custodians of the lands and waters on which we rely. We pay respect to Elders past and present of the lands where we conduct our work and recognise their ongoing contributions as the first educators on the land now known as Victoria.

To find out more about Dance Levels 7–10, watch ‘Understanding the Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0, Dance Levels 7–10’ on the Resources page.

Rationale and Aims

Rationale

Dance is a distinct discipline and body of knowledge within the arts. Dance is expressive movement with purpose and form. Early sensory experiences through play and playful dance are fundamental to students’ learning in Dance and to the development of kinaesthetic and discipline knowledge. Through Dance, students explore the elements of dance, skills, techniques and processes. They question and celebrate human experience, using the body as the instrument and movement as the medium for personal, social, emotional, spiritual, cultural and physical communication. For children in the early years, Dance is play and playful movement.

Like all art forms, dance has the capacity to engage, inspire and enrich all students and excite the imagination. Learning in Dance is inclusive and encourages students of all abilities to reach their creative and expressive potential. Dance develops students’ creativity, imagination, aesthetic knowledge, collaborative skills, communication, confidence, curiosity, problem-solving skills and self-expression.

In Dance, students draw on a diverse range of experiences, sources and ideas for creating dances. Students use the elements of dance to explore and practise technical and expressive skills for choreography and presentation to an audience. As they learn in Dance, students develop a movement vocabulary with which to explore and refine ways of moving both individually and collaboratively. They learn to choreograph, present, perform and appreciate as they engage with dance practices and practitioners from their own and others’ cultures and communities.

Dance as an art form enhances students’ knowledge and understanding of diverse cultures, times and places, developing their personal, social and cultural identity. Dance is a central element in the diversity and continuity of local and global cultures, particularly the cultures of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. Through Dance, students develop an understanding of how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples express connection to and responsibility for Country and Place.

Aims

The Dance curriculum aims to develop students’:

  • capacity as artists and audiences
  • play and playful movement
  • body awareness and technical and expressive skills to communicate through movement confidently, creatively and intelligently
  • choreographic and performance skills and appreciation of their own and others’ dances
  • aesthetic, artistic and cultural understandings of dance in past and contemporary contexts, its relationships with other art forms and its contributions to cultures and societies
  • respect for and knowledge of the diverse purposes, traditions, histories and cultures of dance by making and responding as active participants and informed audiences
  • knowledge of the diversity and significance of dance for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ artistry, cultures and communities.

Structure

The Dance curriculum is presented as one curriculum level at Foundation and then in 2-level bands from Levels 1 to 10.

Foundation Levels A to D for the Arts bring together learning from Dance, Drama, Media Arts, Music and Visual Arts. Foundation Levels A to D curriculum levels are developed for students with intellectual disability and learning delay.

Dance comprises 4 interrelated strands:

  • Exploring
  • Developing Practices
  • Creating
  • Presenting.

Exploring

In this strand, students learn as artists and audiences. They explore:

  • movement and dance ideas, practices and works
  • cultures, times, places and other contexts in which dance occurs
  • dance works and the ways in which they are presented and performed
  • the diversity and significance of storytelling and dance for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ cultures and communities
  • how dance communicates cultural and aesthetic knowledge, ideas and purposes
  • how dance develops understanding of multiple perspectives
  • how to reflect and respond to their explorations using the language of movement and terminology associated with dance.

Developing Practices

In this strand, students develop practices and skills in dance. Initially these practices and skills are achieved through play and imagination. Students:

  • learn about and develop their understanding of the elements of dance (body, time, space and energy), movement categories and expressive, technical and performance skills
  • learn about and develop skills in choreography as the main creative process for making dance
  • learn about the role of music in dance
  • shape their dance ideas using processes such as improvising, exploring, reimagining, selecting and structuring movement to communicate their intentions
  • develop practices associated with production elements such as costume, props, set, sound, lighting, make-up and technologies
  • develop skills to critically observe, reflect, respond, analyse and evaluate their own and others’ practices in dance using the language of movement and terminology relevant to dance
  • develop skills in safe, inclusive and sustainable dance practices including appropriate use of the body, performance space, technologies, production elements and inclusion of others.

Creating

In this strand, students are positioned as artists. As artists, students:

  • use the elements of dance, expressive and performance skills, and movement categories to make and create dance works as individuals and in groups
  • use choreographic processes to create original, devised dance, or interpretations of others’ dances
  • consider and select music and sound
  • create dances that may be work in progress or may be rehearsed, refined and realised for presentation, in both formal and informal settings, to an audience
  • observe, critically reflect on and respond to their own and others’ creative practice using the language of movement and terminology relevant to dance
  • use safe dance practices.

Presenting

In this strand, students as dancers share work and ideas with audiences in ways that are safe, inclusive and appropriate to the work and its intentions. Presenting includes performance and considers:

  • how students plan, select, choreograph and rehearse
  • audiences as real or virtual, small or large, peers or invited and intentional audiences
  • presenting or performing dances in and for diverse spaces
  • use of additional materials and technologies such as the production elements of costume, props, set, sound, music, lighting, make-up and technologies
  • the process of reflecting on and documenting their responses to their own and others’ dance works using dance terminology
  • use of safe dance practices.

Achievement standards

Achievement standards describe what students are typically able to understand and do, and they are the basis for reporting student achievement.

Foundation Levels A to D for the Arts provide a developmental continuum with the first achievement standard at Foundation Level A, and then at Foundation Level B, Foundation Level C and Foundation Level D.

From Foundation in Dance, students progress along a learning continuum that provides the first achievement standard at Foundation, and then at Levels 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.

Content descriptions

In Dance, content descriptions sequence and describe the knowledge, understanding and skills that teachers need to teach and students are expected to learn.

Elaborations

Elaborations are examples that provide guidance on how the curriculum may be transformed into a classroom activity or learning opportunity. They are provided as advisory material only.

Learning in Dance

Elements of dance

Each arts discipline, including dance, has its own elements. Elements are the foundational building blocks of knowledge and skills in dance.

The elements of dance are:

  • body
  • time
  • space
  • energy.

The elements of dance work dynamically together to create and communicate ideas and intentions through dance to audiences. Other dance terminology may be included, particularly at Levels 9 and 10, for example elements of dance to align with senior secondary courses.

Types of dance

In the Dance curriculum, students learn about dance from a range of cultures, times, places and other contexts. They explore, choreograph and perform dances that are drawn from diverse styles and forms that are representative of the 3 main types of dance:

  • dance created/choreographed to be performed to an audience (for example, forms of theatrical dance such as ballet, tap and jazz; exhibition dance such as ballroom dance; local dance traditions, storytelling dance, dances that depict traditional practices and folk dance; and dance choreographed for screen-based works such as films or games)
  • participatory dance for personal and social purposes not intended for a broader audience (for example, dance for exercise, social dance styles, dance crazes or novelty dances)
  • dance performed or participated in for a specific purpose such as spiritual devotion or ceremonial rites (for example, dance in traditional celebrations or festivals or as part of a cultural ceremony such as a wedding).

Viewpoints

Throughout their Dance learning, students use questions based on viewpoints as an inquiry tool for considering their own and others’ use of ideas and concepts from multiple perspectives. Students can use questions based on viewpoints to:

  • structure their reasoning and reflecting
  • explore ideas and make decisions
  • explore and develop empathy for multiple perspectives
  • express and celebrate identities, ideas and meaning
  • think deeply about their own dance practices and about dance works they experience that are created by others.

As they create and respond to dances and experiences, students develop questions to explore ideas, perspectives and meaning. They think and make decisions as artists and as audiences. Questions based on viewpoints encourage students to consider a range of perspectives and to think deeply about their own dance and the dances created by others.

Contexts

The context of a dance work is the frame of reference that allows its meaning to be interpreted. Interpretation of the meaning of a dance work can evolve from the context in which it is created, and the location and time in which the dance is presented or viewed. Contexts can also be the economic, philosophical, historical, social or cultural influences on the practices of the artist, the artist’s intentions, and the intended communication of ideas, values and beliefs.

Artists

In dance, artists include dancers, choreographers, producers, dance notators and other creative practitioners who work in dance contexts to create dance, tell stories and explore artistic, social, political and cultural themes and ideas through movement.

In dance, artists work individually and collaboratively using historical and contemporary styles and choreographic processes to create dances. Students investigate the practices and dance works of artists working in diverse forms across cultures, times, places and other contexts, including the works of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

Safe dance practice

Safe dance practice encourages and promotes physical health and emotional wellbeing. It includes physical and psychological dimensions and should be applied at all times in Dance learning. Safe dance practice includes warming up and cooling down the body, wearing clothing that enables the body to move freely, awareness of bodies and objects in a dance space, and the creation of safe and collaborative spaces for students to feel included.

Materials and technologies

Movement is the essential material of dance. Movement begins with the body and body awareness, including the use of body bases, body parts and body zones. The body uses movement vocabulary developed by using the elements of dance to express and give form to feelings and ideas in choreography and performance. Additional materials and technologies can be applied.

In dance, additional materials enable:

  • creation of setting(s); for example, using open-ended materials such as recycled materials, lengths of paper, and large and small boxes to create or represent a space
  • communication of place; for example, using a length of material to represent a river, or specific set pieces to move around and interact with
  • communication of a character within a dance; for example, using a costume item or prop
  • symbolism and representation; for example, using coloured fabric or rostra blocks of various heights to enable levels and indicate power and status
  • communication of time; for example, using props and costumes to indicate the period of the performance or dance style.

In dance, technologies enable:

  • on-screen viewing of live or recorded dance from diverse cultures, times and places to broaden awareness of the possibilities of the art form or to support dance ideas and processes of analysis
  • stimulus prior to developing dances using screen-based images, sound or music
  • using technologies and online platforms to assist with production and production elements
  • reflection on, evaluation of or refinement of work in progress; for example, using video of a rehearsal to consider refinements and next steps in the dance
  • use of available devices to support reflection and responding; for example, capturing a gesture or travel sequence and asking students (as audience) to reflect on whether the intended meaning is being communicated
  • use of projections (text or still/moving image) to contribute to or juxtapose with live action to enhance the meaning in a dance
  • use of lighting (including torches or handheld LED lights)
  • use of sound and music, including recorded sound and music, to create and manipulate mood or atmosphere and to support the dancer.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Dance - Foundation Level A (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level A, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for sensory exploration and experiential approaches that enable arts learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level A, students explore and develop practices through the Arts disciplines by participating in and interacting with arts experiences, elements, materials and/or technologies.

Learning in the Arts involves exploration together with structured learning opportunities appropriate for the learning needs of individual students.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level A, students experience and attend to arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They participate in the co-creation of arts works and contribute to the sharing of arts works with others.

Dance

Students interact with the elements of dance to develop an understanding of movement.

Drama

Students interact with the elements of drama and expressive skills.

Media Arts

Students interact with media arts forms, language and/or technologies.

Music

Students interact with the elements of music and instruments.

Visual Arts

Students interact with art elements and materials.

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering ways of using body percussion to explore rhythm and sound, for example by clapping or tapping

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an interest in sounds or the representation of sounds in their environment, for example by attending to a musical sound or vibration by turning their head or body as the sound or sensation travels or by associating music with routines such as musical cues for the start and finish of activities or the school bell

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in multisensory opportunities to explore music practices such as by listening or feeling, experimenting or playing instruments

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to associate sounds or vibrations with their source, for example by touching a drum in response to a sensation

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of art equipment, for example by holding various objects, mark-making tools and materials for short periods of time

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to a visual artwork to explore ideas, for example by reaching towards, touching or exploring objects, environments, colour, texture or materials

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and interacting with two- or three-dimensional artworks that have been created using digital technologies and tools, such as images, soundscapes, interactive artworks, public art or screen-based works

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring artworks made by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people to develop an awareness of the culture and practices of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists

elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sound, smell and feel of various objects, reacting to the sensory stimulus and making artwork as a response to the experience

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAD01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: participate in arts experiences using elements, materials and/or technologies

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing a performance space, as both a performer and audience member

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of props, costumes and sounds as part of play to support movement

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a range of fundamental movements to music, for example by bending, stretching, twisting, turning (non-locomotor), crawling or moving up and down (locomotor)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring movement through repeated patterns

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing a reaction to a situation, using their preferred communication modality

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing a performance space, as both a performer and audience member

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring props, costumes, puppets and sounds as part of dramatic play and process drama, for example engaging with and handling props, costumes and puppets or engaging with a puppet using expressive skills such as facial expressions, gestures, movement and/or vocalisations

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and responding to sound in drama such as the sounds of rain and wind, transport or animals

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing media technologies being used to capture images and sounds for stories

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring different ways of using media arts works, for example by taking samples of images or sounds they react to and integrating sounds, images or objects to represent their preference or their responses

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with the use of a digital camera to capture still or moving images, for example by using a switch, clapping to activate and deactivate a camera or viewing or reacting to images created using the effects of a ‘photo booth’ camera application

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the use of software to create a photo story about themselves

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of a change in elements of music such as duration or dynamics, for example by placing their hand on an instrument that is played softly and then loudly or by turning their head in response to a beat that is slow and then becomes fast

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring instruments by using an instrument, responding to the touch of an instrument or holding and using an instrument with assistance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the accompaniment of chants, songs and/or rhymes using their preferred communication modality or an instrument

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing music for different purposes, for example by using music as a cue for transition, relaxation or movement or to reflect different settings and feelings

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating a preference for art elements such as colour, shape and texture, for example by choosing similar textures, colours or shapes

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in sensory experiences that provide opportunities to explore sights, sounds, smells, tastes and textures and to enjoy and appreciate visual arts materials, techniques and processes, for example by manipulating and exploring the feel of art materials such as clay

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with different materials, techniques and technologies and reacting to the interaction or result

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with the qualities and properties of materials such as paint, crayons, clay and found objects and showing a preference for or communicating what they would like applied to their visual arts works, for example by showing excitement when paint and a paintbrush or roller is on a table or when an easel is set up with a canvas, ready for painting

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAC01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: contribute to the co-creation of arts works

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing and responding to concepts through their preferred learning modalities such as visual, kinaesthetic, auditory or tactile

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in sensorimotor experiences, using gentle movements and interactive play to explore different textures and rhythms

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising movements with support to begin to develop technical skills of body control, posture, strength, balance and coordination

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to rhythmic cues or showing an awareness of a movement they have made

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to choose an object to be included in a dance such as a piece of fabric or a prop

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing tactile and sensory stimuli to evoke a sense of place in a drama work, for example by smelling or feeling seaweed, pampas grass or sand or listening to recorded sounds of the sea during a drama work about a seaside location

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the use of props, costumes and sounds to contribute to a performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding when things that interest them are being used in a dramatic performance, for example smiling when their favourite music is played as part of a performance or reaching out to a favourite prop being used

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity such as exploring sounds, images and text to contribute to a shared media arts work such as an animation or class presentation in response to an event or experience, for example being part of a presentation to their school on a class activity or a response to a story

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving shapes or icons on a screen to create a media presentation

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an artwork after experimenting with images and texts in response to a story about an animal or imaginary creature

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the creation of a presentation in response to a film they have viewed with the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to the variety of sounds that can be created with voice and body percussion, for example by listening to, watching or feeling the vibrations of sound effects

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in and attending to the use of sound effects to accompany stories, rhymes, games and pictures, for example participating in choosing and attending to the kinds of sounds that complement these activities

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an object, equipment or instrument to contribute to a group song, for example by activating a switch to play a sound, striking a drum or pressing keys on a musical keyboard

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing an interest in experimenting with making sounds using voice and body percussion, for example by imitating interesting sounds made by another, repeating interesting sounds they discover or showing some creativity in using their voice and body to make sounds

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity, exploring materials to contribute to a shared visual artwork in response to an event or experience, for example returning from a community walk and exploring colours, shapes, textures and objects that could contribute to a group artwork and then expressing ideas about what was experienced on the walk (such as crunching leaves, texture of bark and colours)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving objects or images to create an artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity to repurpose materials into a shared artwork based on experimentation, for example using cardboard or objects that create sound and expressing ideas about an imaginary animal or object

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a visit to an exhibition or art gallery and expressing ideas about the artworks using different materials, sounds or gestures

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAP01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: participate in their arts works being presented

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the presentation of their dance in a digital format

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing a recording of their movement or contribution to a dance work (individual and group efforts), for example listening to an audio recording or viewing a video or photograph of their performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: reacting to an audience when they are performing, for example by changing their expression when they hear or see familiar adults

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing their engagement in a drama work with others in the classroom, for example by interacting with props and puppets or by responding to their teacher in-role

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a role alongside others, supported by staff in the role, for example by participating in a class or school performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: reacting to an audience when they are performing, for example by changing their expression when they hear or see familiar adults

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the presentation of their drama work in a digital format

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sharing of a media arts work that they have contributed to, such as in a digital display in the classroom or school corridor or shared with the class as a reflection and feedback opportunity (such as at a school assembly or on the school website)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing images that represent an experience or ‘tell a story’

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating a reaction to an event or experience by using sounds and images

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a class presentation of an event or experience around a topic, for example by using sounds, gestures or movement in response to a learning experience, class outing or excursion

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness that others listen to and respond to their voice or sounds

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: having their sound contribution recorded and played back to them and the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of being involved in performing for others, for example by responding to the clapping of others

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sharing of their visual artwork, such as in a display in the classroom or school corridor or shared with the class as a reflection and feedback opportunity (such as at a school assembly or sent home to families)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to express ideas about work they have created with another person

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to their artworks being shown in a digital presentation, for example by using sounds, gestures or movements when an image of their artwork is displayed on a screen

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a review of a presentation of class artworks and indicating their feelings about the artworks, for example by using sounds, gestures or movements to indicate their preferences for artwork features such as subject, elements and emotions

elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to the sensory elements of dance such as the movement of a dancer, a prop used, clothing worn or music played

elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to dance works created by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring characters and settings through images, sounds and multimodal texts, for example by listening to a soundscape of the ocean while experiencing textural elements of water and sand

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAD01 - The Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing a performance space, as both a performer and audience member

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of props, costumes and sounds as part of play to support movement

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a range of fundamental movements to music, for example by bending, stretching, twisting, turning (non-locomotor), crawling or moving up and down (locomotor)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring movement through repeated patterns

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing a reaction to a situation, using their preferred communication modality

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing a performance space, as both a performer and audience member

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring props, costumes, puppets and sounds as part of dramatic play and process drama, for example engaging with and handling props, costumes and puppets or engaging with a puppet using expressive skills such as facial expressions, gestures, movement and/or vocalisations

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and responding to sound in drama such as the sounds of rain and wind, transport or animals

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing media technologies being used to capture images and sounds for stories

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring different ways of using media arts works, for example by taking samples of images or sounds they react to and integrating sounds, images or objects to represent their preference or their responses

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with the use of a digital camera to capture still or moving images, for example by using a switch, clapping to activate and deactivate a camera or viewing or reacting to images created using the effects of a ‘photo booth’ camera application

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the use of software to create a photo story about themselves

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of a change in elements of music such as duration or dynamics, for example by placing their hand on an instrument that is played softly and then loudly or by turning their head in response to a beat that is slow and then becomes fast

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring instruments by using an instrument, responding to the touch of an instrument or holding and using an instrument with assistance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the accompaniment of chants, songs and/or rhymes using their preferred communication modality or an instrument

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing music for different purposes, for example by using music as a cue for transition, relaxation or movement or to reflect different settings and feelings

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating a preference for art elements such as colour, shape and texture, for example by choosing similar textures, colours or shapes

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in sensory experiences that provide opportunities to explore sights, sounds, smells, tastes and textures and to enjoy and appreciate visual arts materials, techniques and processes, for example by manipulating and exploring the feel of art materials such as clay

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with different materials, techniques and technologies and reacting to the interaction or result

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with the qualities and properties of materials such as paint, crayons, clay and found objects and showing a preference for or communicating what they would like applied to their visual arts works, for example by showing excitement when paint and a paintbrush or roller is on a table or when an easel is set up with a canvas, ready for painting

as_extracts.name: ARTSFA-E07
as_extracts.description: Students interact with art elements and materials.

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAE01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: engage with arts works and arts experiences by different people and communities

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of the movement of themselves or others, for example giving fleeting attention to movement as they experience a dance performance or smiling when their wheelchair is moved to music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving parts of their body in response to musical sounds, for example swaying, rocking, moving their feet, making facial expressions, vocalising, making mouth movements, bouncing or moving their arms or legs

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to the sensory elements of dance such as the movement of a dancer, a prop used, clothing worn or music played

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to dance works created by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to moments of interest and focusing on a shared point of interest, for example by showing fleeting interest in a brightly coloured and textured cloak worn by others in role-play or attending or responding to changes in performance such as lighting changes or the commencement of music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in and responding to opportunities to explore the sensory experiences of drama, including sights, sounds, smells and textures of drama, for example choosing preferred items from a selection of sensory materials such as fabrics, objects, crunchy paper, a shaker or water in a bottle

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: being supported to engage in aspects of dramatic role-play or process drama of a recent experience or event, for example during the re-enactment of a bus journey with the teacher in the role of the bus driver, students sitting behind in rows, the sounds of the bus and being rocked gently in a chair

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to the collective experience of a dramatic performance as an audience member, for example when experiencing a dramatised familiar short story or puppet show at school or during an excursion

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring characters and settings through images, sounds and multimodal texts, for example by listening to a soundscape of the ocean while experiencing textural elements of water and sand

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring media arts works created by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in the use of technologies to capture images or sounds, for example by using a switch or button to activate media equipment to capture an image or to record a sound

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to composition by attending to images and/or sounds when given a choice or having their vocalisations recorded and compiled into a co-created artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering ways of using body percussion to explore rhythm and sound, for example by clapping or tapping

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an interest in sounds or the representation of sounds in their environment, for example by attending to a musical sound or vibration by turning their head or body as the sound or sensation travels or by associating music with routines such as musical cues for the start and finish of activities or the school bell

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in multisensory opportunities to explore music practices such as by listening or feeling, experimenting or playing instruments

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to associate sounds or vibrations with their source, for example by touching a drum in response to a sensation

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of art equipment, for example by holding various objects, mark-making tools and materials for short periods of time

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to a visual artwork to explore ideas, for example by reaching towards, touching or exploring objects, environments, colour, texture or materials

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and interacting with two- or three-dimensional artworks that have been created using digital technologies and tools, such as images, soundscapes, interactive artworks, public art or screen-based works

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring artworks made by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people to develop an awareness of the culture and practices of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Dance - Foundation Level B (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level B, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for sensory exploration and experiential approaches that enable arts learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level B, students explore, develop practices and contribute to creating through the Arts disciplines by participating and engaging in arts experiences, elements, forms, materials and/or technologies.

Learning in the Arts involves exploring ideas in arts works from different people and communities, within structured learning opportunities appropriate for the learning needs of individual students.

Students contribute to the co-creation of group arts works in response to a shared experience or observation.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level B, students engage with arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They participate in the co-creation of arts works that explore ideas and they identify their contribution to the presentation of arts works to others.

Dance

Students engage with the elements of dance to develop personal movement.

Drama

Students engage with the elements of drama and expressive skills to develop characters, situations and/or settings.

Media Arts

Students engage with media arts forms, language and/or technologies.

Music

Students engage with the elements of music and instruments to develop sounds.

Visual Arts

Students engage with art elements and materials.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Dance - Foundation Level C (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level C, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for the design of structured experiences for students to engage in sensory exploration and the practical application of arts approaches that enable learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level C, students explore ideas communicated through the arts works of different people and communities. 

Learning in the Arts involves students developing practices in the disciplines and communicating ideas through the use of art elements, forms, materials, technologies or techniques.

Students create and share their arts works in informal settings such as the classroom.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level C, students respond to arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They create arts works and present these to others.

Dance

Students explore the elements of dance and production elements to develop dance works.

They use their bodies, objects and/or materials when responding to personal experiences to create dance works.

Drama

Students explore stories and the elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas to develop drama works.

They use elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas when responding to personal experiences to create drama works.

Media Arts

Students explore media arts forms, language and technologies to construct media arts works.

They use media languages, processes and technologies when responding to personal experiences to create media arts works.

Music

Students explore sound sources, instruments and elements of music to develop music works.

They use elements of music and instruments when responding to personal experiences to create music works.

Visual Arts

Students explore art elements, materials and techniques.

They use art elements, materials and techniques when responding to personal experiences to create visual arts works.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Dance - Foundation Level D (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level D, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for the design of structured experiences for students to engage in sensory exploration and the practical application of arts approaches that enable learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level D, students explore how ideas are represented in a variety of ways by different people and communities.

Learning in the Arts involves students developing practices in the disciplines and communicating ideas by experimenting with different art elements, forms, materials, technologies or techniques.

Students share meaning through their creation of arts works and share their arts works with familiar people.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level D, students respond to stories, observations and ideas about arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They create, share and present arts works with others.

Dance

Students explore the elements of dance and production elements to develop dance works that represent ideas.

They use movement and elements of dance to communicate ideas in dance works.

Drama

Students explore the elements of drama, expressive skills and production elements to develop drama works that represent ideas.

They use elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas to represent characters and settings to communicate ideas in drama works.

Media Arts

Students use media languages, processes and technologies to construct media arts works and to represent ideas and stories.

They develop and present media arts works that represent ideas and stories to audiences.

Music

Students explore sound sources, elements of music and instruments to develop music works that represent ideas.

They use elements of music and instruments to communicate ideas and meaning in music works.

Visual Arts

Students respond to ideas in visual arts works and explore art elements, materials, techniques and processes to develop arts works that express ideas in different arts forms.

They use art elements, materials, techniques and processes to communicate their ideas in arts works in different arts forms.

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation, learning in Dance builds on the Victorian Early Years Learning and Development Framework and each student’s prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for play-based approaches that integrate arts learning experiences across the Arts disciplines and/or specialist teaching. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline and examples that span across the disciplines.

In Foundation, students explore dance and learn about how they can dance. They share their dance with peers and experience dance as audiences. The starting point for learning in Dance is play and everyday movements. Students learn about dancing safely and become aware of their bodies’ movement capabilities. They explore movement possibilities using body, time, space and energy. As audiences, they observe how other dancers communicate through movement.

In Foundation, the focus is on students:

  • exploring:
    • dance present in their lives and communities
    • ways of moving and using the body through play, and when responding to music/sounds they hear
  • developing practices in:
    • body awareness and fundamental movement and expressive skills
    • ways to move safely
  • creating:
    • dance sequences and combining movements that communicate ideas or stories
    • dance sequences that explore some of the elements of dance
  • presenting dances they have learnt and choreographed in informal settings such as in the classroom.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Foundation, students describe experiences, observations, ideas and feelings about the dances they encounter at school, home and in the community, identifying what they enjoy and why. Students develop an understanding of ways their body can move. Students use play, imagination, experimentation and selected dance elements to create dances. Students make and share dances.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 1 and 2, learning in Dance builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students continue to learn through purposeful and creative play and movement in environments designed to foster a strong sense of wellbeing, build confidence and develop their connection with and contribution to the world. Students work individually and in collaboration with peers and teachers, drawing on their imaginations, real-life experiences and stimulus materials to make dance. They are introduced to different music and characteristics of dance styles.

Students explore dance in the range of contexts they experience including at home, school and through family and community events. They have the opportunity to connect with choreographers and dancers who live and work in the community. They use stimulus materials such as images, events, texts, questions and observations as inspiration for their own dance making.

In Levels 1 and 2, the focus is on students:

  • exploring:
    • dance across cultures, communities and other contexts, including examples of dance choreographed and performed by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
    • ways of learning movement sequences and dances safely through moving and listening to music/sounds in games and play
  • developing practices in:
    • improvising and creating movement patterns for performance using fundamental movement skills and safe dance practices
    • observing, reflecting on and responding to dance they experience, including their own dance
  • creating:
    • dance sequences by selecting and combining movements that communicate ideas and intentions using fundamental movement skills, the elements of dance and imagination
    • work that combines dance and other art forms, such as a dance sequence for use in a dramatic retelling of a story
  • presenting dances they have learnt and choreographed in informal settings such as classroom presentations.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 2, students identify where they experience dance. Students describe where, why and how people across cultures, communities and other contexts experience dance. Students demonstrate expressive and performance skills, and the elements of dance to improvise and create dance sequences. Students present their work to audiences in informal settings.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, students make and respond to dance independently, collaboratively with peers and teachers, and as an audience for other dancers’ work. Students extend their awareness of how the whole body can be used to communicate ideas. They explore and experiment with the elements of dance and movement categories, and extend their movement and physical skills.

Students experience dance from a range of cultures, times, places and other contexts, and explore how these dances use the elements of dance and expressive skills to communicate ideas and tell stories. They also explore the social and cultural contexts of dances they create, perform and view, including works by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. They connect with choreographers and performers who live and work in the community, for example by experiencing live or virtual performances. They use stimulus materials, such as images, events, texts, questions and observations, as inspiration for their own dance making.

In Levels 3 and 4, the focus is on students:

  • exploring:
    • works and experiences that showcase where, why and how dance is choreographed and performed across cultures, times, places and other contexts; for example, participating in dance events or learning dances choreographed for a specific purpose
    • examples of dance choreographed and performed by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people that communicate connection to and responsibility for Country and Place
  • developing practices:
    • by building skills in choreographic processes, fundamental movement skills, the elements of dance and movement vocabulary using safe dance practice
    • such as observing, reflecting on and responding to dances they experience, including their own dances
  • creating dances by selecting and combining movements and structuring dance sequences that communicate ideas and intentions using fundamental movement skills and the elements of dance, drawing on a range of stimulus materials such as texts, poems, songs, soundscapes and images
  • presenting dances they have learnt and choreographed in informal settings, such as spaces within the school.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 4, students identify and describe how they use movement to create and/or make dances. Students recall and describe where, when, why and how dance is created and presented across cultures, times, places and other contexts including the work of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. Students experiment with the elements of dance when devising dances or learning dances by other artists. They apply safe dance practices, and use the elements of dance and a range of movements to communicate ideas, perspectives and meanings. Students present and share their dance work in informal and formal settings to different audiences.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 5 and 6, students make and respond to dance independently and collaboratively with their peers, teachers and communities. Students further develop their awareness of the body, control and accuracy of body actions and movement categories and understanding of safe dance practice. They extend their ability to manipulate the elements of dance and use compositional devices to create more complex movements.

Students continue to use stimulus materials such as images, events, texts, questions and observations as inspiration for their own dance. These experiences support students to develop aesthetic knowledge across cognitive, sensory, emotive and physical domains and to value artworks and practices from many cultures, including those of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

As they create and respond to dance as artists and audiences, students develop their awareness of how dance can communicate ideas about the past, present and future, different environments and cultural contexts.

In Levels 5 and 6, the focus is on students:

  • exploring:
    • dance from many cultures, times, places and other contexts that shows how the elements of dance can be used to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning
    • dance that showcases Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ dance practices and the role of dance within culture
    • production elements and how they can enhance dance works
  • developing practices:
    • such as creative practices for choreography and performance using safe dance practice, fundamental movement skills, the elements of dance, choreographic processes, spatial production, imagination andprocesses such as improvisation that allow them to extend and refine their movement capabilities
    • such as an understanding of rehearsal process, including practising, remembering and refining their movement and interpretation
    • in observing, reflecting on and responding to dance they experience, including their own dance
  • creating:
    • ideas and structuring movements to create dances that communicate their intentions as choreographers
    • dances that combine dance and another art form
    • dances as individuals, in pairs or in groups, drawing on different stimuli as inspiration
  • presenting dance works they have learned and created in informal and formal settings including to peers, a class or other audiences.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 6, students explore the elements of dance, dance movement and structures, and explain how they are used in creating and learning dances. Students describe how dance is created and presented across different cultures and contexts to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning. They identify how dance is used to continue and revitalise cultures, including the works of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. Students document their ideas and understanding of how the elements of dance are used to create dances. They work individually and collaboratively to create dance works, using the elements of dance, choreographic processes and safe dance practice. They present their dance works in informal and formal settings, identifying different audiences.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 7 and 8, learning in Dance builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students learn in and through the 4 strands to extend their knowledge of choreographic processes, the elements of dance, and performance and expressive skills as well as performing and exploring. They use dance and choreographic processes in purposeful and creative ways, and continue to develop their connection with and contribution to the world as artists and audiences. They work individually and in collaboration with peers and teachers.

As artists and audiences, students learn about dances from a range of cultures, times and places. They learn about style and choreographic intent and how dance communicates story and context. As they make and respond to dance, students analyse and evaluate choreographers’ intentions and the physical and expressive skills in dances they view and perform. Students explore dance specific to contemporary and historical styles, and dance from differing contexts such as dance in countries or regions of Asia, and the works of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. They take opportunities to engage with living performers and choreographers, and expand their awareness of the diversity of dance practices and dance styles.

In Levels 7 and 8, the focus is on students:

  • exploring:
    • the elements of dance, physical, performance and expressive skills, and choreographic processes employed in a range of dance works by performers and choreographers, and dance practices across cultures and contexts
    • a range of music/sounds to accompany dance
    • production elements and how they can be used to enhance dance works
    • the choreographic work of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples with respect to and consideration for Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property (ICIP) rights
  • developing practices:
    • to build and refine physical and expressive skills and their own movement vocabulary using safe dance practices
    • to manipulate the elements of dance to create new dances and recreate existing dances
    • such as analytical skills in order to respond to their own and others’ dance works and use the language of movement and dance terminology
    • such as an understanding of rehearsal processes, including practising, remembering and refining their movement and interpretation
  • creating:
    • dance works to communicate ideas/intentions using the elements of dance and choreographic devices, and referencing different styles and their accompanying conventions and techniques, incorporating production elements such as costume, props, set, lighting and sound
    • dance works that respond to their own interests and experiences
  • presenting and performing their dance works in informal and formal settings including to peers, a class or other audiences in the community or beyond.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 8, students analyse how the elements of dance and production elements are manipulated to create dance works. Students describe ways dance works from a range of styles and across cultures, times, places and other contexts communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning, including the works of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. They identify and describe how and why respectful approaches are used in creating, recreating and responding to dance works. Students select, apply and demonstrate an understanding of styles and techniques in dance. Students document and reflect on their dance practice using dance terminology. Students manipulate the elements of dance, drawing on safe dance practices to create works that communicate ideas, viewpoints and meaning. They plan, rehearse and present their dance works to a range of audiences in both formal and informal settings.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 9 and 10, learning in Dance develops students’ capability and confidence across the dance practices including the elements of dance, physical and expressive skills, choreography, performance and critical responding. They continue to use choreographic processes in purposeful and creative ways. At these levels, students are informed by their engagement with the work of choreographers and performers from across local, regional, national and global cultures, times, places and other contexts, including the work of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists.

In Levels 9 and 10, the focus is on students:

  • exploring:
    • choreographers’ and performers’ use of the elements of dance, choreographic devices, selected style techniques and production elements across cultures, times, places and other contexts
    • ways in which dance choreographed and performed by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people celebrates and challenges multiple perspectives of Australian identity
  • developing practices:
    • by building and extending creative practices for performance and choreography, considering prior learning, safe dance practice, experience and interests
    • by building and extending critical practices through taking opportunities to reflect on and evaluate their own work, and respond to and analyse the dance works of other choreographers applying movement language and dance terminology
  • creating:
    • dance to communicate ideas and intentions using the elements of dance and choreographic devices that are appropriate to the selected genre/style
    • by employing physical and expressive skills to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning in their dance work
  • presenting:
    • their work using physical and expressive skills that reflect specific dance techniques to communicate their ideas and intentions to audiences
    • their work to specific audiences and identifying who that audience is and in what space they are presenting.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 10, students analyse and evaluate how the elements of dance, choreographic devices and style-specific techniques are manipulated in dance they create and present to audiences and in works they experience. They evaluate how and why choreographers across contexts and cultures present and challenge ideas and meaning through dance. They evaluate how dance is used to celebrate and challenge perspectives in relation to Australian identity, including the dances of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. Students work individually and collaboratively to create dances that communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning. They document, reflect on, analyse and evaluate their own and others’ work using relevant dance terminology. They use production elements to enhance their dance making in both devised and learnt dance works. Students select and manipulate the elements of dance, style-specific techniques and choreographic devices to structure dances for audiences, adhering to safe dance practices. Students plan, rehearse, refine, present and perform dances to a range of audiences in a range of settings, both informal and formal.

organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2ADA10D01 - Dance
strand_content_descriptions.text: experiment, develop and refine the elements of dance, physical and expressive skills, and style-specific techniques to communicate meaning, adhering to safe dance practices

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D01-E01 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking viewpoint questions, such as ‘What content am I planning on including in my dance?’, ‘What am I learning about techniques and processes when creating this dance?’, ‘Why is this dance working out successfully?’ and ‘What am I doing creatively?’

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D01-E02 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with and refining physical and expressive dance skills in response to stimulus materials, such as a theme or narrative, and making choices in the creation of the dance

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D01-E03 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing and refining skills in relation to control, accuracy, strength, balance and focus while preparing a section of a dance that is devised

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D01-E04 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing and refining physical skills to develop proficiency in style-specific techniques such as ballet, jazz, tap, lyrical, hip-hop, contemporary and others

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D01-E05 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing dance works that specifically focus on the elements of dance, the use of the body, time, space and energy, and describing the use of each of these elements

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D01-E06 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: working with a peer to evaluate and document the use of safe dance practices such as warming up the body, preparing the space and considering physical skills, and asking viewpoint questions such as ‘What will I need to think about?’

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2ADA10D02 - Dance
strand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on, analyse, evaluate and document their own and others’ dance works to inform choices and interpretations they make as dancers, choreographers and audiences

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D02-E01 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: using questions based on viewpoints to reflect on and evaluate the use of the elements of dance, such as ‘How can I use and manipulate the elements of space and energy to convey my ideas?’

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D02-E02 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating choreographic and performance choices, for example by asking questions such as ‘How successful were the dancers in conveying the choreographer’s stated intent?’ or ‘What was the impact of the performer’s choice to use gesture to communicate emotion?’

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D02-E03 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: documenting creative processes in a written, pictorial or digital journal

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D02-E04 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ‘analyse’ and ‘evaluate’ as command terms to assist in writing about their own or others’ work

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D02-E05 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing movement choices that reflect their individuality and to clarify their choreographic intent

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10D02-E06 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing a seen work, either live or digital, and recording the use of the elements of dance, identifying choreographic processes, describing the intention and evaluating the effectiveness of the work for an audience

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2ADA10C01 - Dance
strand_content_descriptions.text: create and choreograph dance using the elements of dance, choreographic devices and style-specific techniques to communicate ideas and convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C01-E01 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking viewpoint questions, such as 'What am I learning about this technique or style?’, ‘How does my work communicate my original ideas?’, ‘What changed during the process?’, ‘Why did I decide to make those changes?’ and ‘How can I use and manipulate the elements of space and energy to convey my ideas?’

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C01-E02 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: using choreographic devices to create an original dance work that represents a theme such as peace, conflict, reconciliation or change

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C01-E03 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a new dance work that draws on works of artists from different cultures, times and places, and adapting dance ideas to create movements that represent a synthesis of influences and present a personal meaning or perspective, using respectful dance practice

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C01-E04 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating movement motifs in imaginative ways to communicate their choreographic intent for an audience

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C01-E05 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: working with a group to create a new dance work where movement vocabulary is shared to represent a theme or idea

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2ADA10C02 - Dance
strand_content_descriptions.text: apply production elements to dance works to enhance meaning for an intended audience

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C02-E01 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: using costume to define a character within a dance

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C02-E02 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying production elements to enhance the meaning of a created dance, for example a prop to symbolise strength

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10C02-E03 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying specific music choices to represent the intended meaning of a dance

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2ADA10P01 - Dance
strand_content_descriptions.text: rehearse, refine, present and perform original dance works or learnt dance works to audiences in a range of settings, both formal and informal

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10P01-E01 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning how they can use the performance space in ways that are consistent with style, mood or ideas conveyed in a dance; for example, beginning in the audience, beginning in ‘the wings’, beginning on stage or involving the audience within the presentation

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10P01-E02 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: using available production elements such as music, costume and props to enhance communication of ideas, perspectives or meaning in a performance

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10P01-E03 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: using rehearsal processes to refine their dances for presentation or performance to an audience

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10P01-E04 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: using production elements such as projection, soundscape, music, special effects or voice overs to explain and identify the intention of a dance for an audience

elaborations.name: VC2ADA10P01-E05 - Dance
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrate safe dance practices throughout their presentation, including warm-up and cool-down, awareness of space and surfaces, and use of appropriate clothing and footwear
